gaps.note: The held copy of Cisco's support page "Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches" has no entry for the Nexus 9504, and no end-of-sale notice for the chassis is held, so its sale status is unknown. The 9508's entry on the same page says nothing about it.
gaps.wanted: the Nexus 9504's status on Cisco's support page, or an end-of-sale notice for N9K-C9504

gaps.note: The guide gives a typical and maximum draw per module and no figure for the chassis itself; the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Each line card carries its own typical and maximum draw, so a loaded chassis's total is the sum of its occupants; none is written here.
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the sum of the module table is the answer

gaps.note: Which fabric module each line card goes with, and how many are needed, is listed here and NOT ENFORCED: no bay or card restricts the fabric module it is seated with. The guide's Overview Table 1 (PDF pp8-9, printed 2-3) pairs the cards modelled here with the N9K-C9504-FM-E (this chassis has no FM-E2) and the N9K-C9504-FM-G; the count is the fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth. N9K-X9736C-FX: FM-E 5, FM-G 5. N9K-X97160YC-EX: FM-E 4, FM-G 4. N9K-X9732C-FX: FM-E 4, FM-G 4. N9K-X9716D-GX: FM-G 4 only. The guide's notes: FM 5 (slot 25) works only with the N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9736C-FX3; the -G fabric modules need the N9K-C9504-FAN2 fan trays and take N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR in empty slots; all fabric modules in the switch must be of one type; and "Do not mix ACI-mode line cards with NX-OS mode line cards in the same switch" (PDF p7, printed 1). "Migrate the switch to 400-Gigabit -GX line cards" (PDF p118, printed 112) says to replace the older fabric modules with "N9K-C9508-FM-G" modules, a sentence copied from the 9508 guide.
gaps.wanted: a restriction in the format between a card and the fabric modules it is seated with

gaps.note: The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19; callout 14 in the table on PDF p26, printed 20) gives the width of the chassis plus the vertical mounting brackets as 19.2 in (48.8 cm). The ear model has no field for an overall width, so the mounting-bracket region is not sized by it and the front face stays the 444.5 mm chassis width.
gaps.wanted: ear support for an overall width, or a dimensioned front view of the bracket

gaps.note: The guide's rack kit is N9K-C9504-RMK (two bottom-support rails and 20 each of M6, 10-32 and 12-24 screws; PDF p31, printed 25), with the accessory kit N9K-ACC-KIT (printed N9K-C9500-ACK in Appendix C, PDF p139, printed 133). The library has a kit contract for the N9K-C9500-RMK only, and listing it here would break lint while it says `unplaced:`. The 9504's own kit is not modelled and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: a follow-up that adds the N9K-C9504-RMK kit and lists the kits on the 9504, 9508 and 9516

gaps.note: The guide's DC supply procedures say "Verify that the Input 1 (IN1) and Input 2 (IN2) LEDs light up on the power supply" (PDF p43, printed 37, and p117, printed 111), but its Power Supply LEDs table lists only OK and FAIL (PDF pp137-138, printed 131-132), and the shared N9K-PDC-3000W-B draws OK and FAIL only. The IN1 and IN2 lamps are not drawn, and the supply is not edited here.
gaps.wanted: the position and colours of the DC supply's IN1 and IN2 lamps, drawn in a new version of the supply

gaps.note: The guide says an even slot (FM 2, FM 4, FM 6) must hold a fabric module to power the fan tray in front of it (PDF p118, printed 112; fan-tray lamps, PDF p135, printed 129, which lists only the FM, FM-E and FM-S), and names a blank only for the odd slots (N9K-C9504-FM-CV) and, for the FM-G, N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR for any empty slot. It names no N9K-C9504-FM-Z; "N9K-C950x-FM-G-Z" in the migration caution is the 9508's text copied. What fills an empty even slot with a non-G fabric module is therefore unknown, and no part is made.
gaps.wanted: what Cisco ships to fill an empty FM 2, FM 4 or FM 6 with the N9K-C9504-FM, -FM-E, -FM-S or -FM-R

gaps.note: The guide's own planning table (PDF p18, printed 12) gives the N9K-C9504-FM-R 130 W in the maximum column and 140 W in the typical column. A typical draw above the maximum cannot be right, and lint refuses it, so the part carries the 130 W maximum as printed and no typical figure.
gaps.wanted: the N9K-C9504-FM-R's typical and maximum draw from Cisco's data sheet or a corrected guide

gaps.note: The four supplies lie in two rows of two either side of the centre panel and the guide numbers them "left to right" (PDF p10, printed 4), which does not say which of a vertical pair is PS 1. PS 1 and PS 2 are put in the left pair (PS 1 on top) and PS 3 and PS 4 in the right pair (PS 3 on top), by estimate.
gaps.wanted: a figure that labels the four slots, or the slot numbers printed beside them

gaps.note: The guide says a blank module sits in an empty supervisor or system-controller slot ("remove the blank module that is already in that slot. Unscrew its captive screw", PDF p85, printed 79, and p89, printed 83) and gives it no part number, drawing or dimension. The supervisor and system-controller bays therefore show nothing when empty.
gaps.wanted: the part number and a drawing of the supervisor and system-controller slot blanks

gaps.note: The guide has no flat front or rear elevation, and the NetBox elevations are not held. Every position on both faces is derived from the dimension table and the arrangement in the isometric figures; see the front-stack and rear-stack provenance. No position is measured.
gaps.wanted: a flat front and rear elevation of the chassis with dimensions, or the NetBox elevation images

gaps.note: The bay sizes are the module envelopes of the dimension table, and the positions are the stack derived from them; none is a measurement of the chassis. The fan-tray bays and the fabric-module bays occupy the same area of the rear face because the fabric modules are behind the fan trays.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view with the fan trays removed

gaps.note: The side and top faces are named in the figures (handles on both sides, mounting bracket, rack rail positions) and no figure dimensions any feature on them, so those faces carry regions with no coordinates. The bottom face is empty: no view of it is published.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side and top view

airflow.note: datasheet - "Air intake from the cold aisle for all modules and power supplies" and "Air exhaust to the hot aisle" (clearance figure, PDF p25, printed 19, callouts 4 and 5; table on PDF pp25-26), and "port-side intake airflow" for every supply. The chassis is front-to-back.

chassis.note: datasheet - Appendix A "Switch Dimensions" (PDF p119, printed 113): "Cisco N9504 chassis: width 17.5 inches (44.5 cm); depth 33.15 inches (84.20 cm) for chassis and handles; height 12.25 inches (31.1 cm) (7 RU)". Modelled as 444.5 x 311.15 x 842.0 mm. CONFLICT ON HEIGHT: three places say "7.1 RU (12.4 in [31.6 cm])" instead - Rack and Cabinet Requirements, "the 7.1-RU (12.4 inches or 31.6 cm) height of the switch and its bottom support bracket" (PDF p24, printed 18); the bottom-rail step, "at least 7.1 RU (12.4 in [31.6 cm]) of vertical space above the rails" (PDF p32, printed 26, with callout 2 on PDF p33, printed 27); and the chassis-install checklist (PDF p34, printed 28). The text counts the bottom support bracket and the space above the rails, which the table does not, and 12.25 in is 311.15 mm, exactly 7 x 44.45 mm; the table (7 RU, 311.15 mm) is used, and it is also what the front stack adds up to. The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19, callout 11) gives the same 33.15 in (84.2 cm) depth as the table, so depth has no conflict here. Chassis weight 84.0 lb (38.2 kg), PDF p120 (printed 114).

chassis-lamps-position.note: estimated - CONFLICT ON WHERE THE CHASSIS LAMPS ARE: Appendix B "Chassis LEDs" (PDF p133, printed 127) says they are "located at the top of the front of the chassis"; the front figure (PDF p10, printed 4, callout 5) puts them on the centre panel between the power supplies, at the bottom of the face. The sentence is the same in the 9508 and 9516 guides, whose faces do have the lamps at the top. The figure is drawn from, and the text is recorded. The legends BCN, SUP, FAB, IOM, PSU, FAN and PWR MGMT are plain text as the guide prints them; the vendor logo and wordmark above them are not drawn, and a logo-zone is reserved.

ears-and-kits.note: drawing - the clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19) shows the chassis between front and rear vertical rack posts with its front at the front posts, and the front figure (PDF p10, printed 4, callout 4) shows "2 vertical mounting brackets used to mount the chassis onto a rack" at the sides of the front. The rack-mount step (PDF p37, printed 31) pushes the chassis on until "the vertical mounting brackets on the front of the chassis come in contact with" the rack's vertical rails. The shipped position is therefore flush, and no `at` is written: no figure gives the bracket's depth position. The clearance figure (PDF p25, printed 19; callout 14 in the table on PDF p26, printed 20) prints "Width of the chassis plus vertical mounting brackets on each side" as 19.2 in (48.8 cm), against the 17.5 in chassis: about 21.6 mm of bracket on each side. The ear model takes a depth offset and a height and no width, so that span is carried here and in a gap, not drawn. A rear-mount position is not given by the guide. The shipment list (PDF p31, printed 25) names "Rack mount kit for the Cisco N9504 (N9K-C9504-RMK) chassis" - two bottom-support rails and 20 each of M6, 10-32 and 12-24 screws - and the "Switch accessory kit (N9K-ACC-KIT)"; Appendix C (PDF p139, printed 133) prints the accessory kit as N9K-C9500-ACK, holding the same bottom-support rails kit plus a ground lug kit and cables. N9K-C9504-RMK is not the N9K-C9500-RMK that the 9508 and 9516 guides name. The rack must be a four-post rack 24 to 32 in (61.0 to 81.3 cm) deep between its front and rear rails (PDF p24, printed 18; the rails' span again on PDF p32, printed 26). No kit is listed under `chassis.kits`: a listed kit that still says `unplaced:` fails lint, and removing the sentence edits a shared kit, so the kits are a follow-up pull request.

environmental.note: datasheet - Appendix A "Environmental Specifications" (PDF p119, printed 113), transcribed. CONFLICT ON ALTITUDE: the "Altitude Requirements" paragraph (PDF p14, printed 8) says 10,000 ft (3048 m), and 6,562 ft (2000 m) for China; the Appendix A table says 0 to 13,123 ft (0 to 4,000 m). The table is used, and the paragraph is recorded here.

fabric-slots.note: datasheet - "Overview" Table 1 and the note beneath it (PDF pp8-9, printed 2-3): three fabric modules go in FM 2, 4 and 6; four in FM 2, 3, 4 and 6; five in FM 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 or alternatively FM 2 to 6; five FM-E in FM 2 to 6; six in FM 1 to 6. CONFLICT: "Installing a Chassis" (PDF p31, printed 25) says five modules "must be in" FM 2 to 6 only. Both are carried; the slots accept any module and the pairing is not enforced. With the N9K-C9504-FM or -FM-E "any empty slots should be filled with N9K-C9504-FM-CV"; with the -FM-G they take N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR (PDF p9, printed 3); FM 1, FM 3 and FM 5 left empty take N9K-C95xx-FM-CV and FM 2, FM 4 and FM 6 are filled "with fabric modules to power the fan trays" (PDF p118, printed 112). The guide names no N9K-C9504-FM-Z: the one "-Z" it prints, "N9K-C950x-FM-G-Z" in that migration caution, is the 9508 guide's text copied and no part is made from it. Where an even slot is empty with a non-G fabric module the guide does not say what fills it (a gap). FM 5 (slot 25) works only with the N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X9736Q-FX and N9K-X9736C-FX3 and not with other line cards (PDF p9, printed 3): of the line cards modelled here, only the N9K-X9736C-FX. That is not enforced (see the gap line-card-fabric-pairing). An empty odd slot defaults to the FM-CV.

front-stack.note: estimated - every position on the front is derived, not measured. The guide's front figure (PDF p10, printed 4) is an isometric drawing, so no aspect check (Gate 1) can be made, and its numbers are not scaled. The arrangement follows that figure and the dimension table: four line cards of 1.75 in (44.45 mm) stacked top to bottom from the top of the face, centred in it as the 17.0 in (431.8 mm) cage; the two supervisors, 1.75 in high and 8.0 in (203.2 mm) wide with brackets, side by side; then four power supplies of 5.25 in (133.35 mm) by 1.75 in (44.45 mm) lying flat in two rows of two, one pair at each side of a centre panel. The arithmetic closes: 4 x 44.45 + 44.45 + 2 x 44.45 = 311.15 mm. In the figure (fig-0007, PDF p10) the supervisor row and the supply row both reach the line cards' left and right edges, so each row is inset 0.25 in (6.35 mm) from the chassis edge like the cards, estimated by laying the figure's row ends against the card ends. The two supervisors keep their own 8.0 in width (the part is shared with the 9508 and 9516 and is not changed): SUP 1 stands at the cage's left edge and SUP 2 at its right edge, which leaves a 1.0 in (25.4 mm) gap between them, not at the right end. The supplies stand at the cage's edges and the panel between them is 17.0 - 2 x 5.25 = 6.5 in (165.1 mm) wide. The supplies are the shared parts, drawn standing on end, so each bay turns its supply by 270 degrees: in the figure the grille is at the outer end, the power receptacle and handle at the inner end, and the two small lamps at the lower outer corner, which is what a quarter turn of the part (grille at the top, receptacle at the bottom, lamps top left) gives. Which supply of each pair is PS 1 is not shown: PS 1 and PS 2 are put in the left pair (top, bottom), PS 3 and PS 4 in the right pair, as the guide numbers them left to right and puts PS 1 and PS 2 on grid A (PDF pp78 and 80, printed 72 and 74). The seven chassis lamps are read from the figure's centre panel, which carries them in a row about halfway down it, at an even pitch measured against the panel's own width.

lifecycle.note: unknown - the held copy of Cisco's support page "Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches", https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/nexus-9000-series-switches/series.html, has no Nexus 9504 entry, so its sale status is unknown (it is not inferred from the 9508's entry on the same page, which says available). Sale status of each module is per module: N9K-C9504-FM and N9K-C9504-FM-S are end-of-sale by notice; the others have no status and are recorded as unknown.

line-cards.note: datasheet - the four line-card slots accept the line-card blank N9K-C9500-LC-CV and the line cards this guide supports among those modelled: N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX, N9K-X9732C-FX and N9K-X9716D-GX, which Overview Table 1 and the power tables (PDF pp8-9 and 17-20, printed 2-3 and 11-14) list. A line card is accepted because this chassis's own guide supports it. The other 9500 line cards follow in later batches; the N9K-X9788TC-FX is listed in the guide and not modelled, because the guides name its 48 ports three ways and no figure of its faceplate is held.

power-slots.note: datasheet - "Overview of Power Modes" (PDF pp77-80, printed 71-74): with grid redundancy PS 1 and PS 2 go to one source (grid A) and PS 3 and PS 4 to the other (grid B); "up to two with the combined power mode, up to three with n+1, or up to four with n+n" (PDF p10, printed 4). The guide contradicts itself on mixing supply types: "The switch can be powered by a mix of AC, DC, and HVAC/HVDC power sources" (PDF p10, printed 4, and p24, printed 18), against "Do not use a mix of AC and DC power sources for a switch" (PDF p123, printed 117). Every supply type is accepted by every slot.

power-tables.note: datasheet - "Planning for Power Requirements" holds two tables. The first (PDF pp17-18, printed 11-12; the copy begins at the foot of p18 and runs to p20, printed 14) is headed with the 9504's own parts and is followed by a copy of the 9508's table, which names N9K-C9508-* parts and carries different figures (its FM-E row is two lines, 570/420 and 455/266). The chassis's own table is used for every module here, and the copy is recorded as a conflict. The worked example (PDF p21, printed 15) counts two supervisor B at 90 W, two system controllers "2 x 26 W = 52 W" (the table says 25 W each, so the example's 26 W is a slip), four line cards at 1050 W, six fabric modules at 504 W and three fan trays at 600 W: 9,256 W. The 9504's FM-R row prints a typical (140 W) above its maximum (130 W); lint refuses that, so the part carries the maximum only and the typical is a gap. The N9K-C9504-FAN-PWR has no row in the 9504's own table; its only row names the 9508's part.

rear-stack.note: estimated - the rear is derived the same way. The guide's rear figure (PDF p11, printed 5) is isometric. Three fan trays of 5.05 in (128.27 mm) are centred across the width, each 10.6 in (269.24 mm) tall with its brackets; the six fabric modules, 2.46 in (62.48 mm) wide and 9.4 in (238.76 mm) tall, sit behind them on a pitch of half a fan tray, so FM 1 and FM 2 are behind FAN 1, FM 3 and FM 4 behind FAN 2, FM 5 and FM 6 behind FAN 3 (the guide says the even-numbered fabric slot is the one behind a fan tray that powers it, PDF p135, printed 129). The two system controllers, 7.81 in (198.37 mm) wide with brackets and 1.42 in (36.07 mm) high, sit below the fan trays. 10.6 in + 1.42 in fit inside the 12.25 in height; the vertical margins and the controllers' horizontal positions are estimated. CONFLICT ON FAN-TRAY WIDTH: 5.05 in (128.27 mm) and 12.81 cm (128.1 mm) are printed in one cell (PDF p120, printed 114), and the 9508 and 9516 guides print 5.04 in for the same tray; the inch figure is used.

ru.note: datasheet - 7 RU, printed in the dimensions table (PDF p119, printed 113). "Maximum of 255 pounds [116 kg]" is the lift-tool requirement, "the full weight of the chassis ... and its installed modules" (PDF p34, printed 28); it is carried as an attribute, not as the chassis weight.

slots.note: datasheet - "Overview" (PDF p7, printed 1, and p10, printed 4): supervisor modules in slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 (modules 27 and 28), system controllers in SC 1 and SC 2, line cards in LC 1 to LC 4 (top to bottom), fabric modules in FM 1 to FM 6 (slots 21 to 26, left to right), fan trays in FAN 1 to FAN 3 and power supplies in PS 1 to PS 4 (left to right). "Slots are numbered from left to right or from top to bottom". Numbering is the guide's; whether each label is printed on the metal is not shown by any figure the guide gives. The Overview list (PDF p10, printed 4) spells the second fan tray "N9K-9504-FAN2": a slip for N9K-C9504-FAN2.

sources.note: Cisco N9504 NX-OS Mode Switch Hardware Installation Guide (140 pp; first published 2014-03-24, last modified 2026-07-30), https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/datacenter/nexus9000/hw/n9504_hig/guide/b_n9504_nxos_mode_hardware_install_guide.pdf (page numbers below are PDF pages with the printed page after them, six lower: "PDF p10 (printed 4)"). Cisco's Nexus 9508 and 9516 hardware installation guides were read to confirm the parts the three chassis share; each chassis cites its own guide. The NetBox devicetype-library file for N9K-C9504 and its elevation images were NOT available to this work - only a path listing of that library is - so no NetBox elevation was compared. No data sheet, photograph, 3D model or stencil is held for the 9504. The guide has no flat front or rear view and prints no figure caption: both faces were read from its isometric figures on PDF p10 (printed 4) and p11 (printed 5).
